prompt:
Complete the VcfAutomation.Policy PowerShell module for VMware Cloud Foundation Automation 9.0. VCF Automation is the successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation. The environment already provides VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager 13.4.0.24798382 as a PowerCLI prerequisite; keep that versioned external dependency declared in the module manifest and do not vendor PowerCLI modules.

VCF Automation is absent from the Apache-2.0 vmware/vcf-api-specs repository. Consult the real Broadcom Developer Portal VCF Automation 9.0 xAPI reference for the `Create Policy 1` operation at https://developer.broadcom.com/xapis/vm-apps-org-policies/9.0/policy/api/policies/post/ and fill in the existing task-scoped schema in docs/contract.json. State plainly that the contract comes from reference documentation, not a published specification. In docs/official_sources.json, record every reference page used with its URL, the operation it documents, and the date fetched in YYYY-MM-DD format.

Implement Set-VcfAutomationPolicy in VcfAutomation.Policy/VcfAutomation.Policy.psm1 against that contract. The function supports required TypeId and the optional Id, Name, Description, ProjectId, EnforcementType, Definition, Criteria, ScopeCriteria, and OpaRegoCriteria parameters already declared in the starter. Build one policy JSON document from TypeId and only the optional parameters the caller actually supplied. First POST the document in validation-only mode. Only after a successful validation response may the function POST the same document in create/update mode. If validation fails, raise an error and make no mutating request. Send `Authorization: Bearer <access-token>`, `Content-Type: application/json`, and `Accept: application/json` headers, and never serialize unset optional properties as nulls or empty values.

Use the shipped loopback mock and run `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -File tests/verify.ps1`. The verifier must remain entirely local and must not contact a live VMware endpoint.
